## Design

### 2026-11-01: The first hour consisted of researching parts and listing everything needed. (Research.md, Requirements.md, and BOM.md)

**10h**

The first hour consisted of researching parts and listing everything needed. (Research.md, Requirements.md, and BOM.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/47e5e4c62cf9dca8694c8e0570ea24e98f1fced361780313a774e611c085a7fa.png)

In hour 2, Mapped out the hardware bus layout. I placed the digitizer and SD card reader on a shared secondary SPI bus (HSPI) with separate chip selects. Calculated memory requirements: a 648x480 1-bit framebuffer requires only 38.8 KB of RAM, meaning the ESP32-S3's 512 KB internal SRAM and 8 MB PSRAM provide plenty of room for multiple buffers and history undo stacks. (Architecture.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/d58bb183eff4980d485bf6de896afb5dd7c552505324f0bcc67f6c7f74968d8b.png)

In hour 3, I built the electrical power tree schematic. Connected an 1800 mAh LiPo cell to a TP4056 USB-C charging IC paired with a DW01A protection IC to prevent over-discharge below 3.0V. (Electrical.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/c5bc7ec2a9066282efbdca776f47a5d6674ca15e46bc92b32943523921b0c689.png)

 In hour 4, I drafted the complete GPIO routing table for the ESP32-S3. Avoided known strapping pins (GPIO0, GPIO45, GPIO46) that could accidentally force the board into bootloader mode on startup. (Pinmap.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/3c604a00af5afb765516d347c6ef5cb439d865329396b5f062618aa9bf7a7cec.png)

In hour 5, I mapped out the UC8179 command sequences. Documented the full global refresh sequence (3.5 seconds, clears ghosting) versus the partial refresh sequence (300 ms window updates for typing and pen strokes). (Display_Digitizer.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/2e13cf0e6a96a476fa008c5b4496dcea596524568795efb06e5b65ebc3826e8e.png)

In hour 6, I created the bridge between the raw digitizer coordinates and the actual display pixels. (Calibration.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/b2a6ffb5124d5c0e0fc23932452ed7b5ad54326c1a5dec4925cb45717a0916c1.png)

In hour 7,  I built the system power state model. Active drawing pulls roughly 38 mA, giving 45+ hours of continuous note-taking from the 1800 mAh cell. (Power.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/10360bda7ba4998be1484b6fcf5fdb1d840b47cfc6a9a5e0e226ed88b385f6c3.png)

In hour 8, I designed the custom E-Paper Graphic binary vector format. Each file begins with a compact 16-byte header containing file signature, timestamp, resolution, and total stroke count. (Storage.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/ab9f28df0fbf497f5b3539e83876dcc5f70bccaf82c9a6ed378cef30195c862c.png)

In hour 9, I built the UI by placing a thin 32-pixel utility toolbar along the top edge featuring Pen, Eraser, Clear Screen, Page Navigation, and Battery indicators. Defined palm-rejection logic: whenever the stylus tip touches the screen, the system ignores peripheral edge contacts to prevent accidental button presses. (UI.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/b00248b477a94b581900325aee3b1f7688a7dca0809059e131c06bd2d63da226.png)

In hour 10, I wrote a hardware assembly guide for when I build it. It covers battery connector polarity checks, FPC ribbon cable insertion, component placement inside the 3D-printed frame, and first-boot smoke testing using a current-limited bench supply or USB monitor. (Assembly.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/365206fa8b4095288933e5921aa2f6bd6922a5b077ba6f04373d661f725c93ea.png)
